A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–J. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original model-training results, molecular-dynamics simulations and geometry-optimization experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains the original training, simulation and optimization results, including the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The PET variants, conservative fine-tuning and multiple-time-stepping procedures are unchanged. The more explicit abstract summarizes procedures already described in v3 Section 4.8 and Appendices H–I.

E1.justification: Both retain the water experiments, QM9/MPtrj geometry optimization, diverse-material simulations and OC20-based training and surface simulations. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including the PET and SOAP-BPNN variants, ORB, MACE-MP-0, SevenNet and Equiformer.

E3.justification: Training and evaluation settings are retained, including the 15,000/5,000 OC20 training/validation samples in Appendix H, MD ensembles and thermostat settings, and geometry-optimization stopping criteria.

E4.justification: The receptive-range comparison, closed-loop work tests, optimization failure analyses, thermostat and stress tests, velocity-rescaling analysis and MTS sensitivity studies are all retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting in Tables 2, 8 and 9 and the two-standard-error bands in Figures 12, 13 and 17 are unchanged. Neither version adds run-count, seed or statistical-testing information relative to the other.

E6.justification: The reported numerical results and plotted findings match. For example, Table 1 retains force MAEs of 19.4 and 24.8 meV/Å for the jointly energy/force-trained conservative and non-conservative PET models, respectively.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning are retained, including the Jacobian-asymmetry measure, harmonic-mode analysis, computational-cost and receptive-range arguments, and MTS derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract strengthens the hybrid recommendation from an approach that 'might be' best to 'We show that the best approach' uses both force types. It also foregrounds the existing training and inference contributions; the central findings and discussion remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of energy drift, disrupted equipartition, sampling inefficiency and optimization fragility are unchanged, as are qualifications concerning model accuracy, force-field differences and MTS stability limits.

D1.justification: Implementation details, GPU and timing information, model configurations and software versions are retained. The Software and Data section and Appendix J provide the same code, data and example access information.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are unchanged. The comparison with rotational-symmetry breaking remains in the introduction and discussion despite its removal from the abstract.

P1.justification: The closing portion of the abstract is rewritten and expanded to explain pretraining, fine-tuning and combined inference. Several cross-references change from 'Appendix' to 'Section'; the section order and body narrative are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Page reflow moves Table 1 from page 5 to page 6 and the introduction opening to the right column of page 1. Running-title text disappears, while the figures, table structures and appendix layouts remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The abstract now explains direct-force pretraining, conservative fine-tuning and combined inference explicitly, making the constructive contribution easier to understand than v3's broad tandem-model recommendation. This is a limited communication improvement; the unchanged experiments and appendices provide no additional support for the firmer 'best approach' wording.
